title: Income Tax Assessment Act 1997
formulas_sidecar_note: Subdivision 960-M, s 960-275 only, transcribed 2026-10-22 from Volume 10 of the Word rendering of C2026C00400 (REQ-0057); the other formulas the text lost are not transcribed.

symbol_repair_2026_11_07.converter: cth_convert_sym.py (a copy of docx_text() and the volume joining of the workbench converter harvest/fetch/fetch-source.py, earlier tools/fetch/fetch-source.py, changed only to map Word symbol characters; kept outside the repository)
symbol_repair_2026_11_07.from: the same Word volumes, C2026C00400VOL01-12.docx, refetched from the Federal Register of Legislation; joined, they hash to this deposit's download_sha256 (3d56a3f8e0809b7731db16b6d508b66d44d7646d9641bb1b7b7aef4ad5e3faf1)
symbol_repair_2026_11_07.why: docx_text() read only w:t, w:tab, w:br/w:cr and w:noBreakHyphen, so it dropped every Word <w:sym> character, and it kept Symbol-font text typed as private-use code points (U+F0xx), which display as empty boxes. This compilation sets five characters as Word symbols in the Symbol font, all in the two example lines of s 124-790(2): F0B4 (×), F0B8 (÷), F02D (−) and F03D (=) twice; and it has 41 Symbol-font bullets typed as U+F0B7. cth_convert_sym.py maps Symbol-font characters to their Unicode characters (· × − • ≤ ≥ ° ′ — ÷ ± and + = < > ≡), Wingdings boxes to "[ ]", and private-use code points U+F0xx the same way; no Wingdings box occurs here.
symbol_repair_2026_11_07.what_changed: 43 lines, nothing else: line 26291, s 124-790(2) example, "[$100 × $200] ÷ $500 = $40" (was "[$100 $200] $500 $40"); line 26292, "$100 − $40 = $60" (was "$100 $40 $60"); and 41 bullets written as "•" instead of U+F0B7, 39 in the s 30-15 table (lines 5199-5352) and 2 in s 30-315(2) (lines 7044-7045). Line numbers are unchanged, so the formulas sidecar's line references still hold.
